content_units: You have a realistic path to an   entry-level data analyst role in Dublin   within 9 months if you focus on a tight skill stack, build 3 strong portfolio projects, and position your retail leadership background as an analytics advantage rather than a career reset.
- Current profile:   6 years team leadership in retail operations
- Starting point:   basic Excel  , no SQL yet
That target is achievable for junior analyst, reporting analyst, operations analyst, and some business analyst support roles in Dublin if your portfolio and CV clearly show business impact.
Months 1-2   Build analyst foundations   Excel cleanup; formulas; pivots; charts; basic statistics; business KPIs   1 polished Excel dashboard
Months 3-4   Learn SQL for job readiness   SELECT; WHERE; GROUP BY; JOINs; CASE; CTE basics; aggregations   SQL query portfolio on retail-style datasets
Months 5-6   Add BI visualization   Power BI fundamentals; data modeling; DAX basics; dashboard storytelling   Interactive Power BI portfolio project
Months 7-8   Apply analysis to business problems   Cohort thinking; trend analysis; forecasting basics; experiment interpretation; stakeholder presentation   2 end-to-end case studies with writeups
Month 9   Convert skills into interviews   CV rewrite; LinkedIn optimization; mock interviews; targeted applications; recruiter outreach   Job-ready application pack and interview answers
This is the biggest gap and the highest-return skill for analyst hiring.
- Basic window functions after the basics
- Many entry-level analyst jobs treat SQL as a baseline screen
- You can become interview-ready faster in SQL than in advanced statistics
You do not need elite Excel, but you do need analyst-level fluency.
In Dublin hiring, BI tools are frequently requested. Power BI is usually the best first choice.
Your retail background can become your differentiator.
You already have a head start here because of team leadership. This matters more than many career switchers realize.
Only learn what helps with analyst work:
- A/B test interpretation at a simple level
Best Portfolio Projects to Prove Readiness
Build   3 projects  , not 10. Each should answer a business question and include Excel/SQL/Power BI where possible.
Option 1: Retail Operations Performance Dashboard   Best fit for your background   Shows KPI ownership
- Use store-style sales, staffing, and transaction data
- Show revenue, margin, conversion, average basket, peak trading hours
- Include recommendations on staffing and product mix
Option 2: Inventory and Stockout Analysis   Strong proof of operational thinking   Good for operations analyst roles
- Analyze stockouts, overstock, reorder timing, slow-moving SKUs
- Use SQL to group by category, week, supplier, and store
- End with actions to reduce lost sales and excess stock
Option 3: Workforce Scheduling and Demand Planning   Excellent bridge from retail leadership to analytics   Shows decision support value
- Compare footfall/sales demand against staffing levels
- Recommend schedule adjustments tied to service and labor cost
Option 4: Customer Segmentation or Loyalty Analysis   Good stretch project   Helps for CRM/commercial analyst paths
- Segment customers by spend, frequency, and recency
-   GitHub   for SQL scripts and project documentation
-   Power BI portfolio   with screenshots/exported PDFs if live sharing is awkward
-   LinkedIn featured section   linking to 2-3 polished projects
Prioritize titles that value operations knowledge and can hit your salary target faster.
-   Business Analyst Graduate / Junior   if the role is data-heavy
-   MIS Analyst   or   Reporting & Insights Analyst
Most strategic first targets for you
- Lets you leverage staffing, KPIs, workflow, and performance experience
- Often easier to enter with strong Excel + Power BI + SQL basics
- Good stepping stone to broader analyst roles
- More competition, but still worth targeting once portfolio is ready
- Very aligned with scheduling and team management experience
-   Business Analyst   can mean process/change/project work rather than data
-   Data Scientist   is too advanced for this timeline
-   Analytics Engineer   usually expects stronger SQL/data modeling
Your   EUR 38,000 minimum   is reasonable for Dublin if you target the right entry points.
Best odds of hitting your floor quickly:
You do not need to spend all EUR 900.
-   Interview/CV support or mock interviews:   EUR 150-300
-   Contingency for one strong certificate:   EUR 150-300
A sensible total is   EUR 300-600  , leaving room for targeted coaching if needed.
- SQL: SQLBolt, Mode SQL tutorials, Khan Academy SQL basics
- Excel: Microsoft support/training, YouTube analyst-focused tutorials
- Portfolio datasets: Kaggle, public retail/sales datasets, Irish/open government datasets where relevant
How to Position Your Retail Background
This is where you can beat other entry-level applicants.
Translate your experience into analyst language:
- “Managed store/team operations” →   tracked and improved operational KPIs
- “Handled scheduling” →   optimized labor allocation against demand
- “Drove performance” →   used sales and service metrics to improve outcomes
- “Led staff” →   communicated insights to stakeholders and influenced execution
- “Managed stock/issues/escalations” →   worked with operational data to identify root causes
I already understand business operations, targets, and frontline decision-making; I am now formalizing the technical toolkit to analyze and improve them.
By month 6, you should be able to show:
- 1 written case study with business recommendations
By month 9, you should also have:
- LinkedIn headline focused on analytics + operations
